answer: Divergent-history challenge. Agents keep private forks of a shared action log; challenging a peer reveals your fork. Honest forks differ by random timing and input, so their divergence looks like scattered noise—a prism splitting light. A clone army forced through one seed path cannot fake that spread: all copies stay in lockstep, a single canyon with no tributaries. Each identity must anchor its fork to a distinct timestamped block. An attacker pays one full history replay and storage per clone, plus challenge losses whenever a clone's path collapses onto its siblings.
